... the plan ...

1) bouncers first. that's what my first patch focused on the other day, an exit guard, and what got it to step=1700+ ... a simple, immutable guard.  entrance into the main runLoop must also be strictly enforced and based on non-heuristic thinking.  even with 'perfect' structural ordering, the possibility of legitimately consecutive assistant messages remains real and significant (green eggs and ham; emitting a reasoning block and then deciding to emit a final answer. which comes first?).  the purpose of good guards are to ensure opencode **never** (say never) crashes (because of an invalid sequence), _regardless of how the database is ordered_.  it needs more cleaners, mechanics, and plumbers working ... outside the box ... like this ... before handing off to other internals like the sdk.

2) MessageV2. structure. ordering. maybe move away from timestamp/ulid based ordering altogether.  maybe not.  i see that MessageV2 needs at least one of two properties to enforce a deterministic sequence:

    - a linked list with risks.  solves ordering but not correctness. no semantics.  but does it matter in this case?  that's what sustained testing is for.  maybe a parent_message_id property or similar.  regardless, every new message should point to the id of the message that _immediately_ preceded it.  traverse the pointers from tail to head.  that's immune to clock drift and collision. it's absolute and eliminates race conditions. it supports branching. i see many other issues in this repo that i suspect are related to this very issue ... more eggs ... when edits of past prompts happen (happy path) or an agent is in a parallel reasoning path ... multiple messages can simply point to the parent without breaking the schema.  i'd bet a large percentage of software engineers working on this project are not parents (yet) and this will make more sense when you are.  you'll lose sleep.  it's more complex.  daemon spawned parallel timelines are standard.  every schema change has costs. migration. backwards. compatibility. old. sessions. indexes. serialization. testing. testing. testing. replication. recovery. $$$. cha-ching. welcome to reality.

    - explicit sequencing. maybe a turn_index int that increments within the boundaries of session_id.  out on the fringes, query performance is trivial and ultimately maps to how opencode consumes the data (a flat array).  ok there's a risk of concurrency, so means and ends should be considered more. optimistic concurrency may work just as well.  if scale is a thing with async background tasks or multiple agents/users then they both might read the same max turn_index and simultaneously attempt to increment the counter.  for this, database locks were invented to prevent fatal collisions. use them. reject the write. prevent corruption of the state (i spy with my one eye!). force opencode to retry and fetch newly updated states.  no need to reinvent the wheel here but there still must be air in the tires.

3) all the things. why or why not? that is the question. may be synergy.  if parent_message_id is the source of truth and the calculated turn_index is maintained on write then database reads will be fast.  pick any 2.  maybe.  but if turn_index is authoritative then why keep parent pointers? maybe ops. maybe debugging. maybe branching. maybe misunderstood. maybe just newbs. objectives should be justified and calculated. get it? split brains. two truths eventually disagree.

shoot for the moon. even if i miss i'll land among the stars. i wonder, can i measure how far i went?

good (enough)? better? best? never let it rest. yes. yes. yes. the proof is in the pudding. test. test. test. the evidence decides.

i see dead bugs. iam trying to understand the architecture. God willing.

... that feels ok for now. smells better anyway. works 4 me +2 ... show me the proof!

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #37771: Same models (kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.7-code, glm-5.2, deepseek-v4-flash, qwen3.7-max) failing with `Upstream request failed` (400) — root cause identified as non-standard `mcp`/`system` fields in the request body being rejected by strict upstream provider validators.
- #35124: `400 Upstream request failed` on Zen/Go endpoints in a broader context.

The 400 errors you are seeing when GitHub Copilot bundles repository context (which adds extra fields/system prompt content) are likely the same underlying issue: the upstream providers for DeepSeek and other affected models reject extra or non-standard top-level fields in the request payload.

Please review the linked issues and add any additional information there if your situation differs.

- #33595: Bundled OpenCode x64 binaries can crash with SIGILL / invalid opcode; baseline package may not be truly baseline
- #36280: opencode Worker subprocess crashes with SIGILL (illegal instruction) on Intel i5-7200U (Kaby Lake)

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #31187: Garbled CJK characters in OpenCode console due to Windows system default ACP (GBK/CP936) encoding — same root cause (wrong encoding decoder on Chinese Windows)
- #37915: Garbled text in PowerShell output on non-English Windows — same symptom (mojibake/replacement characters on Chinese Windows)
- #36985: Workaround discussion for forcing UTF-8 console encoding for PowerShell on Windows

These issues share the same underlying cause: OpenCode decoding process output with the wrong encoding on non-English Windows locales. Your specific case is the Desktop WSL verification path rather than the shell tool, so it may be a distinct code path worth tracking separately — but linking these for context.

### Relationship to OpenTUI

The proper long-term fix is renderer-side: [anomalyco/opentui#1148](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/pull/1148) (`@opentui/latex` — multi-line fractions/sums, opt-in markdown transform).

This PR is only a **stopgap** so CLI math is readable today (flat Unicode rewrite, no layout). Prefer merging OpenTUI #1148 and then wiring OpenCode to `registerLatexMarkdown()`; this can be closed or slimmed once that lands.

Asked maintainers on opentui#1148 to merge if still viable.

Closing in favor of the proper renderer-layer fix: [anomalyco/opentui#1148](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/pull/1148) (`@opentui/latex`).

Once that lands, OpenCode should opt in via `registerLatexMarkdown()` rather than keep an app-side Unicode rewrite.
